transition_independence_test.interpretation: Anomaly labels ARE dependent on the previous label (Markov property).

leakage_analysis.target_definition: next_anomaly = label of the next segment on the same channel
leakage_analysis.leakage_explanation: The next_anomaly label is derived from the NEXT segment, which is temporally after the current segment. When predicting for a given segment, the features used are only from the CURRENT segment (no lookahead). The next_anomaly label is only used as the TARGET variable, not a feature. Train/test boundary is preserved: test segments predict next-test-segment anomaly. No test label is used as a training feature.
leakage_analysis.boundary_case: The last segment of each channel has no "next" segment — these rows are excluded from the lead-time task (handled by NaN drop).
leakage_analysis.conclusion: Future-event target is constructible WITHOUT leakage.

temporal_classification.label: LIMITED TEMPORAL BENCHMARK
temporal_classification.rationale: Transition matrix shows serial dependence (chi2 test p<0.05), and 275 valid N→A transitions provide lead-time signal. However, anomaly runs are short (most length-1) and lag-1 correlation is weak across channels. Short-horizon prediction is possible but limited.
